name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Sniffer Drone CSD-3
product_name: Carrion Defense Works Chemical Sniffer Drone CSD-3
description: A small quadcopter drone equipped with a hypersensitive chemical analysis suite that can identify specific compounds in the air at parts-per-trillion concentrations. The CSD-3 flies autonomously through designated areas, sampling atmospheric composition and flagging the presence and concentration of explosives, chemical weapons, drugs, biological agents, and specific industrial compounds. The drone can follow a chemical gradient to its source, effectively tracking a scent like a bloodhound. Carrion designed it for CBRN reconnaissance but its use has expanded to law enforcement, industrial safety inspection, and corporate espionage.

specifications.autonomous flight: Programmed search patterns or gradient tracking

story_hooks: A CSD-3 detected trace explosives in the air of a government building — the gradient tracking led to a maintenance closet containing a device that had been in place for weeks, undetected by every other security measure.
A modified CSD-3 has been repurposed to track specific individuals by their unique chemical signature — body chemistry, soap, diet, and medication create a profile as unique as a fingerprint.

physical_description.visual_profile: Compact quadcopter with an aggressive militaristic stance. Four carbon-fiber rotors extend from a central hexagonal body that tapers toward sensor arrays. The frame suggests purposeful efficiency rather than consumer aesthetics—every angle serves detection capability. Integrated sensor cluster dominates the undercarriage, bristling with intake ports and analysis apertures.
physical_description.dimensions: 20 cm rotor-to-rotor span, approximately 12 cm body length, 8 cm height
physical_description.weight_description: Handheld and pocketable at 0.4 kg; easily deployable from a tactical vest or equipment pouch
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite frame with titanium sensor housings, aircraft-grade aluminum motor mounts
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with anodized dark gray accents; non-reflective to minimize visual detection. Sensor ports feature brushed steel bezels. Rotor blades have subtle iridescent coating to reduce turbulence noise signature.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary, charcoal black recesses, steel gray sensor apertures. Minimal accent lighting in cold cyan/electric blue for status indicators.
physical_description.interface_elements: Micro-LED status array on dorsal surface (blue/red/amber diagnostics), recessed docking port on ventral side, three small tactile buttons for manual override, micro-USB charging port, wireless telemetry antenna (nearly invisible), sample collection cartridge bay with quick-release mechanism
distinctive_features: Hypersensitive intake array with four asymmetric ports arranged in gradient-analysis geometry
Rotor blades etched with proprietary serration patterns for silent operation
Integrated spectrographic sensor cluster visible as darkened dome on undercarriage
Pulsing cyan indicator lights that activate during compound detection
Exposed heat-dissipation fins on sensor housing suggesting extreme processing capability
Military-grade finish with no corporate gloss—purely functional aesthetics
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CARRION DEFENSE WORKS embossed on starboard rotor boom (minimal branding), FCC/UEC regulatory stamps on battery compartment, unit serial number etched on frame spine, threat-level diamond warning decal on rotor guard
physical_description.condition_typical: Active unit shows faint chemical residue on sensor apertures from recent deployments, slight propeller wear marks, condensation on lens covers after operating in humid GLMZ environments. Well-maintained units display minimal wear; field-used units show scuffed composite and sensor port patina
